feedback.problem:
Calculate the product $D{I}_{2}$ given that ${I}_{2}$ is the $2\times 2$ identity matrix and
$D=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 3 \\ 2 & 0\end{aligned}].$

| $D\cdot {I}_{2}=\,\,$ |  | {{field-1}} | {{field-2}} |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  | {{field-3}} | {{field-4}} |  |  |
feedback.worked_solution:
Any matrix, when multiplied by an identity matrix, remains unchanged (assuming that the multiplication is well defined).

The matrix $D$ is a $2\times 2$ matrix and ${I}_{2}$ is a $2\times 2$ matrix too. 

Therefore, the multiplication is well defined and 

$$
D\cdot {I}_{2}=D=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 3 \\ 2 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$
